cpuid_faulting.meaning: cpuid at CPL 3 executes and returns the CPUID record; it does not fault (CPUID faulting, MSR_MISC_FEATURES_ENABLES bit 0, is not enabled)
cpuid_faulting.source: level 2 by absence, per the orchestrator's observable-behaviour ruling: (a) MS Learn __cpuid/__cpuidex (cpp/intrinsics/cpuid-cpuidex, read 2026-11-15) documents the intrinsic as generating the cpuid instruction for ordinary programs, its example is a plain user-mode console main() that executes cpuid and prints the result, and no page text mentions a privilege restriction or an exception; (b) Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c is_privileged_instr lines 1214-1271 lists the instructions Wine reports as STATUS_PRIVILEGED_INSTRUCTION (opcode 0x0f 0x20-0x23, in/out, ins/outs, int) and cpuid (0f a2) is not among them; Wine does not use ARCH_SET_CPUID. No pinned source states that Windows 7 SP1 sets the MSR; the SDM Vol 3A pinned here does not describe CPUID faulting (searched 'cpuid faulting': no hit); blocker for a stronger source: Intel SDM Vol 4 (MSRs) and a Windows 7 SP1 statement, neither pinned

em.source: ruling of the orchestrator (each row is what a ring-3 thread observes on the declared OS): x87 executes natively, no emulation trap is visible; derived: CR0.EM = 1 iff PF_FLOATING_POINT_EMULATED is TRUE, MSDN IsProcessorFeaturePresent gives that value the meaning 'floating-point operations are emulated using a software emulator' (WDK 7.1 winnt.h line 8718), the declared value is 0 (processor_features[1]), and MSDN KeSaveFloatingPointState (learn.microsoft.com wdm/nf-wdm-kesavefloatingpointstate, read 2026-11-15) names STATUS_ILLEGAL_FLOAT_CONTEXT 'the system is configured to use floating-point emulation, rather than doing floating-point operations in the processors' as the other configuration; ks386.inc CR0_EM = 0x4 names the bit

mp.why: no pinned source states CR0.MP (ks386.inc CR0_MP is a bit constant only); user mode sees it only through smsw (undecided)

ts.source: ruling of the orchestrator (what a ring-3 thread observes): a ring-3 thread never sees #NM and its FP/SSE state is preserved across context switches; the documentation makes the x87 and SSE state part of the thread context (WDK 7.1 winnt.h line 4135 CONTEXT_FLOATING_POINT '387 state', FLOATING_SAVE_AREA line 4152, ExtendedRegisters line 4275) and no documented user-mode exception for a not-available FPU exists; MS text does not state smsw's TS bit, so this is the observable behaviour only; ks386.inc CR0_TS = 0x8 names the bit

pce.why: rdpmc at CPL 3 needs CR4.PCE = 1; the SDM only defines the bit, the declared CPU's cpuid does not state it, the WDK 7.1 constants name no PCE bit and Wine 9.0 has no rdpmc case

tsd.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr intercepts only the 0F opcodes ['0x20', '0x21', '0x22', '0x23'], so rdtsc (0F 31) runs in user mode; consistent with the owner's decision that rdtsc reads the platform timer

umip.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 2.5 CR4.UMIP: the bit is reserved (setting it is #GP) unless CPUID.(EAX=07H,ECX=0):ECX[2] is enumerated; the declared CPU's max basic leaf is 4 (ports/fnv-nx/verify/cpuid_model.json max_basic @ a3217cd2c604), below 7, so there is no leaf 7 and CR4.UMIP is 0

osfxsr.source: derived: CR4.OSFXSR = 1 iff the declared PF_XMMI_INSTRUCTIONS_AVAILABLE (row processor_features[6]) is TRUE, because MSDN IsProcessorFeaturePresent gives that value the meaning 'the SSE instruction set is available' to the calling process and Intel SDM Vol 3A 2.5 / 13.1 raises #UD for SSE instructions when CR4.OSFXSR = 0; ks386.inc CR4_FXSR = 0x200 names the bit

osxmmexcpt.source: ruling of the orchestrator: an unmasked SIMD FP exception reaches the thread as the documented SEH codes, not as #UD; WDK 7.1 winnt.h line 2030 STATUS_FLOAT_MULTIPLE_FAULTS 0xC00002B4 and line 2031 STATUS_FLOAT_MULTIPLE_TRAPS 0xC00002B5 (MS-ERREF 2.3.1, read 2026-11-15: '{EXCEPTION} Multiple floating-point faults.' / '... traps.'); LEVEL 2 for the mapping from #XM to the code: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c fpe_handler case TRAP_x86_CACHEFLT lines 2058-2066 raises STATUS_FLOAT_MULTIPLE_TRAPS (0xC00002B5); the MS pages name the codes but do not state which SIMD exception maps to which; ks386.inc CR4_XMMEXCPT = 0x400 names the bit

cpumodel.origin: the declared CPU's cpuid as data (CPUREF: verify/cpuref.json + verify/cpuid_model.json); lift/rt/cpumodel.c is generated from it, not a source

sdm.terms: ASM-055 (OWNER 10, per the orchestrator): an MS term such as '32-bit flat mode' means what SDM vol. 3A 3.2.1 defines; ASM-055 was not present in verify/ASSUMPTIONS.json on claude/fnv-nx-clean or claude/port-nsw-un6t9s when read (2026-11-15), so the citation names it as the ruling and the registry entry is owed by the orchestrator
sdm.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Volume 3A: System Programming Guide, Part 1

thread_fp_initial.applies_to: the initial context of every thread, the process's first thread and CreateThread threads alike: the documentation names one initial value with no per-kind difference (the INITIAL_* constants of the thread context)

tss_io_bitmap.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr returns EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION for every in/out/ins/outs form with no per-port test (the instruction set is L3b's sdm_priv_rows.tsv, iopl class, not restated here), i.e. a Win32 user process has no permitted port; the documentation names the TSS I/O map (WDK 7.1 ks386.inc TssIoMapBase = 0x66, PrIopmOffset = 0x6E) and the exception (MSDN EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION: an instruction not allowed in the current machine mode) but states no permitted port for a user process, so it does not contradict Wine (precedence 2); with IOPL 0 (row eflags) every such instruction at CPL 3 is #GP(0), delivered as that exception
